notes.summary: Independently confirmed the frozen book’s exponent-direction error. The corrected larger-exponent formula requires decrease, eventual inclusions, and strong openness. DPS version, normalization, complete pertinent text units, and logarithmic-pole limitations were inspected.
notes.detailedSummary: Elementary polar integration gives I(λ log|z|²)=(z^floor λ), including integer thresholds. At λ=1 the printed union over λ′<λ gives O instead of (z), even for a constant sequence satisfying the relevant approximation hypotheses. The corrected λ′>λ formula follows under precisely stated additional premises. DPS is the bound arXiv math/0006205v2, 10 October 2000; its final equisingular theorem is not substituted for finite prescribed-ideal norms. Whole required literal-LF text units through LF775 were read; publisher identity and whole-PDF visual reading are not claimed.
notes.text:
Use dd^c=(i/2π)∂∂̄ and multiplier weights exp(−u). For u=log|z|² and a nonzero germ of order k, local integrability is equivalent to finiteness of 2π∫₀ᵗr^(2k−2λ+1)dr. This holds exactly when k>λ−1, equivalently k≥floor λ. Hence I(λu)=(z^floor λ), including integer endpoints.

Take the constant sequence u_j=u. At λ=1, I(u)=(z), whereas every 0<λ′<1 gives I(λ′u_j)=O. The smaller-exponent union printed in frozen ch51 LF2013–2059 therefore equals O and is false. This globalizes using G=log|z|²−log(1+|z|²) on P¹: ω+dd^cG=δ₀, sup G=0. Its constant sequence decreases to G, has zero curvature loss, has ideal type (1/m,(z^m)), and satisfies the required larger-to-smaller ideal inclusions. Those hypotheses do not exclude the counterexample.

A separate valid assertion is: if u_j↓u, I(λ′u_j)⊂I(λu) eventually for every λ′>λ, and strong openness holds, then I(λu)=⋃_{λ′>λ}⋂_j I(λ′u_j), stalkwise. Right-to-left follows from one sufficiently late inclusion. Left-to-right follows by strong openness, which places a germ in I(λ′u) for some λ′>λ, followed by u≤u_j. Strong openness is an explicitly declared published analytic input, not proved here. This correction authenticates neither every other assertion in the frozen proposition nor its surrounding regularization prose.

The unchanged source body is preserved in LOCALONLY/ch51-qes-preserves-i-original-body.tex. The main certificate proof avoids either union formula.

The two bound private DPS primaries identify arXiv math/0006205v2, 10 October 2000. PDF SHA256: 50709e54ee90dc7d43a9f6b583137a525bdf2195563e0b30535de970545dfa9a. Text SHA256: 331e3c4d85cc17e22b8b357c1c5ff6ee1fc68a02026094f995285491dd0adf46. Every literal newline record LF404–775 was read in bounded chunks, including whole 2.2.1/2.2.2, Steps 1–4, and 2.2.13. PDF pages 10 and 12 were visually checked; whole-PDF visual reading and publisher-identical 2001 bytes are not asserted.

DPS exp(−2φ) requires φ=u/2. Then I_DPS(mφ)=I_book(mu), i∂∂̄φ=πdd^cu, and πθ+i∂∂̄φ=π(θ+dd^cu). A source curvature loss εω becomes εω/π. Its local 1/(2m) kernel logarithm must be doubled. Remark 2.2.2 expressly warns that the final equisingular step loses logarithmic poles. Step 3’s dyadic almost decrease concerns one fixed cover. Neither statement is silently promoted to the required finite-norm interface.

Full analysis appears in P14.8-paper.tex, argument.md, source-application-ledger.md, and sourcecoverage.md. Rerun a bounded extraction with `python read_bound.py dps 736 775`; extraction success is not mathematical validation.

notes.summary: Proved sufficiency of the explicit finite-norm certificate for every positive real index. Upper tails are quasi-psh, decrease without collapse, and the capped integral test equals exact multiplier-ideal membership. No strong openness or positive mass is used.
notes.detailedSummary: The input convention is the full real array A_c, c>0. Finite prescribed-ideal norms Φ_j at m_j=2^j satisfy vanishing θ-loss and bounded, noncollapsed suprema. Compatibility uses a local ball and constant independent of j and the integer cap R. Increasing finite maxima converge locally in L¹ to their raw supremum; canonical psh representation proves equality almost everywhere with the usc envelope. Decreasing mean-value propagation excludes collapse. DCT in N and MCT in R and j identify the compatibility expression with the extended integral against exp(−cu), realizing every index.
notes.text:
Fix connected compact Kähler X, smooth closed pseudoeffective θ, Kähler ω, and I(cu) defined by local integrability of |f|²exp(−cu). The input is an arbitrary full real array of nonzero coherent ideals A_c, c>0. Integer/full-real equivalence is not assumed.

A witness uses finite holomorphic norm formulas of exactly A_{m_j}, m_j=2^j. One rigid presentation is a finite maximum of (1/m_j)log Σ|g_{j,a,ℓ}|²−ρ_a+(Lβ_a+A)/m_j on fixed nested chart balls. Here dd^cρ_a=θ, the smooth geometric terms are specified, and each finite tuple generates exactly A_{m_j} near the relevant inner compact ball. Boundary gluing must be explicitly justified. Arbitrary unknown bounded or psh corrections are excluded.

Require θ+dd^cΦ_j≥−ε_jω, ε_j↓0, and −B≤sup_XΦ_j≤B. Individual Φ_j need not decrease. Put H_{j,N}=max_{j≤k≤N}Φ_k. For every x,c,f require membership f∈A_{c,x} to be equivalent to existence of a coordinate ball U containing x and C<∞ such that, for every j and integer R≥1,
lim_N ∫_U |f|²min(R,exp(−cH_{j,N}))dV≤C.
The representative is holomorphic near the closure of U. U and C may depend on x,c,f, but not j,R. The N limit decreases and is bounded by R∫_U|f|². At a pole the capped weight is R; simultaneous zeros of f contribute zero. Uncapped products are defined through these caps, avoiding 0·∞.

For fixed j, H_{j,N} is (θ+ε_jω)-psh. It increases with an integrable lower bound Φ_j and a uniform upper bound. Dominated convergence gives local L¹ convergence to S_j=sup_{k≥j}Φ_k. Positivity passes in distributions. Let v_j be its canonical quasi-psh representative. The a.e. inequality H_{j,N}≤v_j implies the pointwise inequality by adding a local smooth potential and recovering psh values through shrinking averages. Thus S_j*≤v_j. Conversely those averages are bounded by local suprema of S_j, giving v_j≤S_j*. Consequently Ψ_j=S_j* is (θ+ε_jω)-psh and agrees almost everywhere with S_j.

The Ψ_j decrease and have suprema at least −B. Their nonempty nested compact sets {Ψ_j≥−B−1} have a common point where the limit is finite. Add fixed local potentials of θ+ε_1ω. Sub-mean values at a point with a common lower bound control negative-part integrals on a ball. Fixed positive-volume compact overlaps supply lower-value points for successive charts; sub-mean values on balls containing the next smaller chart ball propagate the integral bounds. A finite connected chain gives uniform local L¹ bounds. Monotone convergence then gives L¹ convergence of the decreasing sequence to a nontrivial limit. Its usc pointwise representative agrees with the canonical representative by average recovery. Passing curvature positivity with ε_j→0 gives u=lim Ψ_j∈PSH(X,θ). This spells out the ordinary decreasing psh machinery; no net compactness or mass premise is hidden.

For fixed j,R, DCT in N with bound R|f|² gives the integral against min(R,exp(−cΨ_j)), using the raw/usc a.e. equality. MCT as integer R→∞ gives the uncapped integral, possibly infinite. Since Ψ_j↓u, another MCT gives
sup_{j,R} lim_N ∫_U |f|²min(R,exp(−cH_{j,N}))dV = ∫_U |f|²exp(−cu)dV.
The exact local-ball quantifiers therefore give I(cu)_x=A_{c,x} for every positive real c, not merely the witness degrees.

This proves sufficiency and explicit reconstruction from a certificate. It does not by itself prove certificate availability. It imports only the precisely disclosed ordinary canonical psh representation/mean-value premises and measure theory; it does not use strong openness or positive mass. Full reasoning is in P14.8-paper.tex Sections 3–4 and argument.md. Programs do not verify this continuum proof.

notes.summary: Author proof of exact necessity interface R through finite weighted Hilbert generators, relative finite kernel reduction, and exact-potential fixed-cover gluing. Named published analytic inputs have explicit scopes; their complete original-primary validation is unavailable.
notes.detailedSummary: For every θ-psh u, the draft constructs finite global ideal norms of exactly I(mu), with curvature loss O(1/m), uniform upper/noncollapse bounds, Φ_m≥u, and usc upper tails decreasing pointwise exactly to u, including polar points. Generation uses point-pole ∂̄ solutions, Artin–Rees and Nakayama. A coherent product ideal and Fréchet openness yield P≤K≤2P, avoiding uncontrolled finite-reduction constants. Exact θ-potentials give O(1/m) overlap estimates on a fixed cover; known barriers glue finite maxima. OT lower bounds and local uniform mean-value upper bounds prove exact tail equality. The unknown target is absent from certificate tests.
notes.text:
The author claims exact interface R: for every u∈PSH(X,θ), there are finite norm functions Φ_m whose actual local generating ideals are exactly I(mu), satisfying θ+dd^cΦ_m≥−C₀ω/m, Φ_m≥u, uniform upper/noncollapsed supremum bounds, and usc upper-tail envelopes decreasing exactly to u along any increasing unbounded integer sequence. The geometric smooth terms are fixed independently of u. The target is used only to prove existence of finite tuples.

The published ordinary inputs are explicitly scoped: (H) weighted Hörmander ∂̄ solutions on bounded pseudoconvex balls for singular psh W with i∂∂̄W≥i∂∂̄|z|² and finite weighted norm of ∂̄-closed (0,1)-data; (O) point OT extension uniformly on an inner compact subset of a ball, with F(x)=1 and ∫|F|²e^(−W)≤C e^(−W(x)); (N) nonzero coherence of multiplier ideals; (C) compact-open closedness of coherent ideal sections, Cartan B surjectivity of finite-generator coefficient maps on Stein domains, and Fréchet openness of those surjections. Ordinary Artin–Rees and Nakayama are used in holomorphic local rings. These are not new grants of R. Their complete original primary texts are absent from the packet; source-application-ledger.md records that evidence limitation.

Choose fixed nested balls B_a^0⊂⊂B_a^1⊂⊂B_a^2⊂⊂B_a^3, cores covering X, and fixed smooth potentials dd^cρ_a=θ. On a ball D let v=u+ρ and H_m={F holomorphic: ∫_D|F|²e^(−mv)<∞}. Its sections have germs in I=I(mv)=I(mu), since smooth bounded weight changes preserve integrability.

For exact generation, fix x. Artin–Rees gives q with I_x∩m_x^(q+1)⊂m_xI_x. For local g∈I_x choose χ=1 near x with compact support in a local integrability domain. Solve ∂̄h=∂̄(χg) on D using W=mv+(n+q)log|z−x|²+|z|². This is psh with the required strict Hessian. The data avoid x, so their weighted norm is finite. The solution is holomorphic near x. Because v is locally bounded above, integrability with the added point pole forces ord_xh≥q+1; the extra factors are bounded above on D, so h also has the original Hilbert norm. Thus F=χg−h∈H_m and F_x≡g mod m_xI_x. Repeat for finite generators and apply Nakayama. Coherence extends equality to a neighborhood, and a finite cover supplies finite H_m generators on any smaller compact ball.

For the finite norm step, put the span of such a generating tuple first in an orthonormal basis f_ℓ of H_m on a slightly larger concentric Stein ball V. Its first s members generate I on V. Mean-value bounds control evaluation and derivatives on compact sets, so K_m=Σ|f_ℓ|² is continuous and its two-variable kernel series converges normally.

On V×V̄ the coherent product ideal J is generated by f_a(z)f_b*(w), a,b≤s, where f_b*(w)=overline(f_b(overline(w))). The tails T_N=Σ_{ℓ>N}f_ℓ(z)f_ℓ*(w) lie in J by closedness and tend to zero in its induced Fréchet topology. Cartan B makes O(V×V̄)^(s²)→J(V×V̄) surjective and open. Apply openness to the neighborhood in which every coefficient has compact supremum less than δ/s. For sufficiently large N, T_N has coefficients in that neighborhood. On the conjugate diagonal,
0≤K_m−P_N≤(δ/s)(Σ_{a≤s}|f_a|)²≤δΣ_{a≤s}|f_a|²≤δP_N.
Thus P_N≤K_m≤(1+δ)P_N uniformly, including ideal zeros. The tuple still generates exactly I. Take δ=1. No uniform-in-m division estimate or generator bound is assumed. This relative reduction is essential: an uncontrolled domination constant C_m would leave a log C_m/m gap.

For fixed-cover overlap estimates, choose a uniformly small ball about an inner overlap point x. Closedness of θ makes ρ_b−ρ_a pluriharmonic, hence Re t for holomorphic t there. Transfer χF exp(mt/2) to the destination ball using H with W=m(u+ρ_b)+n log|z_b−z_b(x)|²+|z_b|². The identity
|F exp(mt/2)|²e^(−m(u+ρ_b))=|F|²e^(−m(u+ρ_a))
is exact. Cutoff derivatives, the point-pole factor on its annulus, and coordinate Jacobians have uniform geometric bounds. The solution vanishes at x. The destination section has value F(x)exp(mt(x)/2) and norm bounded by a geometric multiple of the source norm, independently of m,u. Evaluation suprema and reverse transfer give
C^(−1)K_{m,a}e^(−mρ_a)≤K_{m,b}e^(−mρ_b)≤CK_{m,a}e^(−mρ_a).
Finite relative reduction changes the ratio by at most 2. Therefore q_{m,a}=(1/m)log P_{m,a}−ρ_a obey the extended overlap inequalities with error D/m, D=log(2C), including common zeros. No varying-cover almost decrease is assumed.

OT gives q_{m,a}≥u−log(2C_O)/m on inner balls; at u=−∞ the lower bound is trivial. Mean values give q_{m,a}(x)≤sup_{|z_a(y)−z_a(x)|<r}u(y)+M_ρr+[log C′+2n log(1/r)]/m, uniformly at nearby points. Set A=log(2C_O). Choose β_a=1−|z_a|²/(r_a^1)², at least 3/4 on the cores and zero at patch boundaries, and L=4(D+1). A core branch dominates every boundary branch on a neighborhood, including ideal zeros by the extended comparisons. Define Φ_m as the finite maximum of q_{m,a}+(Lβ_a+A)/m. This proves global gluing with exactly I(mu). Two-way holomorphic generator comparisons prove the same ideal-norm type for the maximum, with its specified finite bounded correction.

Each q branch satisfies θ+dd^cq≥0. The known barriers cost at most LC_βω/m, and finite maxima preserve this common bound. The shift gives Φ_m≥u. A fixed small radius in the upper estimate gives a uniform upper bound, and the lower supremum bound follows from Φ_m≥u.

For fixed x and nearby y, uniform coordinates give Φ_m(y)≤sup_{B(x,C₁r)}u+C₂r+[C₃+2n log(1/r)+A+L]/m. Pass to an upper tail and its usc regularization, then let its starting degree tend to infinity and r decrease to zero. Upper semicontinuity makes the resulting upper bound tend to u(x), including polar points, where every finite upper threshold holds on a sufficiently small ball. The lower bound is u pointwise. Hence the tails decrease exactly to u everywhere. Their quasi-psh status follows from n2’s envelope argument. This proves R; n2’s integral identity then supplies necessity of the compatibility test.

The full proof is in P14.8-paper.tex Section 5 and argument.md. Independent review should scrutinize the coherent-product Fréchet reduction and exact-potential L² transfer. Original-primary source closure of the imported H/O/N/C theorems is not asserted. Neither execution nor DPS hashes verify this continuum proof.

notes.summary: Explicit finite P¹ certificates, incompatible formal arrays, and an independent Cantor/Jensen proof preserve the raw-I mass obstruction. The bounded exact program passed 847 assertions; it does not verify continuum analytic theorems.
notes.detailedSummary: For u=aG, finite binomial tuples yield exactly the prescribed ideals O(−floor(am)D) and norms (floor(am)/m)G. Dyadic coefficients converge monotonically, giving smooth unit and divisorial zero-mass examples. Three arrays fail index monotonicity, subadditivity, or strong openness; the ceiling-minus-one array satisfies the first two constraints but misses the integer threshold. A nonatomic thin Cantor measure has a Green potential whose scaled multiplier ideals are all units and whose raw masses equal 1−s, spanning [0,1]. P-envelope distinctions require a separate theorem.
notes.text:
On P¹ use ω=dd^c log(1+|z|²), D={0}, and G=log|z|²−log(1+|z|²). For 0≤a≤1, u=aG is ω-psh and I(cu)=O(−floor(ac)D), by the exact radial condition k>ac−1, including integer thresholds.

Put q_m=floor(am). The finite tuple sqrt(binomial(m−q_m,ℓ))z^(q_m+ℓ), 0≤ℓ≤m−q_m, generates exactly (z^q_m). Its squared norm is |z|^(2q_m)(1+|z|²)^(m−q_m). Its corrected logarithm is Φ_m=(q_m/m)G. In the infinity chart use sqrt(binomial(m−q_m,ℓ))w^ℓ, including 1; the formulas agree globally. Dyadic q_m/m increase to a, so Φ_j decrease exactly to aG, with zero loss and suprema zero. The n2 identity supplies all-index compatibility. At a=0 this gives the smooth unit array. At a=1 every finite norm is G, the ordinary current is δ₀, and its degree-one nonpluripolar product is zero. Background θ=0 with u=0 supplies another unit-array zero-mass example. No mass division occurs.

Incompatible nonzero coherent arrays on P¹ are: (i) O(−D) for c<1 and O for c≥1, violating A_d⊂A_c for d>c; (ii) units for c<1 and O(−D) for c≥1, violating A₂⊂A₁²; (iii) O(−(ceil c−1)D), which satisfies monotonicity and subadditivity because ceil(c+d)−1≥ceil c+ceil d−2, but has 1∈A₁ and 1 outside every A_{1+δ}. The second example uses the disclosed DEL subadditivity theorem, the third the disclosed Guan–Zhou strong openness theorem. Both are applied after smooth local psh corrections, which leave ideals unchanged. By n2 none can have a certificate.

For the raw obstruction, build endpoint Cantor intervals with ℓ₀=1, ℓ_k=exp(−4^k), and Bernoulli measure μ giving level-k intervals mass 2^(−k). It is nonatomic, and their intersection F has area zero. For x∈F, a containing interval supplies mass 2^(−k) within distance ℓ_k. Layer-cake integration yields ∫−log|x−p|dμ(p)≥Σ(4^k−4^(k−1))2^(−k)=∞.

Let V=∫G_p dμ for the squared chordal Green kernel. Uniformly finite negative area integrals of G_p give V∈L¹ and ω+dd^cV=μ by Fubini. Reverse Fatou and integrated sub-mean values identify the integral with its canonical usc representative. It is finite and smooth off F and −∞ on F, proving F polar without an imported capacity formula.

For u_s=sV, 0≤s≤1, the current is (1−s)ω+sμ. Fix c,x. Nonatomicity permits a small disk whose doubled disk has μ-mass β<1/(cs), if cs>0. The far potential is bounded below. Jensen bounds the near exponential by β^(−1)∫|z−p|^(−2csβ)dμ_near(p), which has finite area integral uniformly in p because csβ<1. If β=0 there is no near contribution. Smooth chordal corrections are bounded. Hence every I(cu_s) is the unit ideal. For s>0 the finite locus is X minus F; there the current is (1−s)ω. Degree-one truncations therefore give nonpluripolar mass 1−s, while s=0 gives mass one. A single full real I-array contains every raw mass in [0,1]. Raw representatives and mass cannot descend, even after normalization. A P-envelope distinction needs the separate P-envelope mass-preservation theorem and is not silently inferred.

The fresh program verify_examples.py passed 847 exact assertions for example-input.json: rational radial thresholds, binomial identities, dyadic coefficients, the bad union direction, ceiling inequalities, and Cantor summands. These are exhaustive only for the saved finite loops. The continuum conclusions are the arguments above. Rerun `python verify_examples.py`; detailed output is example-output.json. Full calculations appear in P14.8-paper.tex Sections 7–8 and argument.md.

notes.detailedSummary: Combining n2 and n3 gives an iff criterion for arbitrary all-real coherent arrays, with no unknown target in its tests. notes.text:
The author claims a complete solution of the specified arbitrary-formal-data alternative: for connected compact Kähler X, smooth closed pseudoeffective θ and Kähler ω, an arbitrary full real array of nonzero coherent ideals A_c is realizable as I(cu), c>0, by a nontrivial θ-psh u if and only if it has the explicit finite prescribed-ideal norm certificate stated in n2.

Proof: n2 constructs the decreasing usc upper-tail limit from any certificate, proves noncollapse and θ-psh positivity, and identifies the capped test exactly with multiplier-ideal membership for every positive real index. Conversely n3 proves exact interface R for every realization: Hilbert sections generate precisely I(mu), finite relative reduction retains kernel estimates, exact smooth θ-potentials give fixed-cover O(1/m) gluing, and local uniform estimates give upper tails decreasing exactly to the original u, including poles. The n2 integral identity then proves compatibility. Thus necessity and sufficiency are both established in the draft; R is not assumed from working305 or the DPS final theorem.

The input is the bare ideal array and geometry. Witnesses quantify over finite holomorphic norm expressions with fixed known geometric smooth terms and explicit curvature/scalar/integral conditions. No target psh variable or arbitrary bounded/psh correction appears in the tests. The target is used only to prove witness existence. This is a noncircular infinite functional-analytic characterization in the stated witness sense. It is not a finite algorithm or effective algebraic axiom system. Independent review must assess correctness, originality, and satisfaction of the intended formal-data alternative; a stronger effective-algebraic interpretation is not solved.

The theorem imports precisely scoped ordinary published Hörmander, point OT, Nadel coherence, and coherent-sheaf/Cartan B inputs, plus ordinary psh and local algebra machinery. Their complete original primaries are absent. Full original-primary source closure is therefore explicitly unvalidated. This is the remaining source-evidence gate, not a concealed assumption of R. The coherent-product Fréchet reduction and exact-potential L² transfer particularly require independent scrutiny. Program or compilation success establishes neither.

The raw output can depend on witness norms. Normalization does not imply certificate independence; canonical normalized I-model recovery would require a separately validated I-envelope theorem. n4 independently retains the raw mass/representative obstruction. No P-type recovery, general all-semivaluation formula, additional zero-mass DXZ interval, or probability normalization is asserted. n1 preserves and separately refutes the frozen bad formula. P14.1/P14.4/P14.5/P14.6 remain separate open targets. P16.4’s editor and acceptance counts were untouched.
